question: Can updating only changed GATE pieces and incident pairs reduce transition cost while a periodic canonical rebuild bounds accumulation history?
scope: Research-only prototype, no search routing or production evaluator changes, no training or checkpoint writes.
rebuild: Initially, after64 changed placements, or whenever more than8 squares change. Canonical full sums for both perspectives.
oracle: Three forward/reverse/forward passes of preserved game transitions and CP diagnostic positions; compare raw and integer results with original full recomputation. Maximum allowed empirical raw error1e-9 and no integer differences.
timing: 100000 paired warmup transitions, eight balanced old/new samples,200000 transitions/sample, game transitions only. Same stored sequence.
limits: One BelowNormal process, ActiveProcessorCount=1,768MiB; pause tournament admission at a batch boundary before compiling/running; resume frozen protocols afterward.
decision: No adoption from speed alone. A promising result requires adversarial rounding/transition tests, search parity, whole-search cost and an explicit numerical-error/fallback strategy. Negative or negligible benefit closes this prototype without changing production.
